clause.heading: 1. Incorporation of Recitals. The Recitals set forth in Paragraphs A through C, above, are incorporated herein as though set forth in full.

clause.text: 2. Appointment. SIERRA hereby appoints ENVISION as its exclusive distributor for the Product in any blend with Krill Oil within the Territory subject to ENVISION fulfilling the terms and conditions of the best efforts marketing requirements set forth herein in Sections 4, 5, and 9. SIERRA shall cease making sales to any customer or distributor who, during the term of this Agreement, violates ENVISION's exclusivity.
clause.heading: 2. Appointment. SIERRA hereby appoints ENVISION as its exclusive distributor for the Product in any blend with Krill Oil within the Territory subject to ENVISION fulfilling the terms and conditions of the best efforts marketing requirements set forth herein in Sections 4, 5, and 9. SIERRA shall cease making sales to any customer or distributor who, during the term of this Agreement, violates ENVISION's exclusivity.

reviews.rationale: The clause creates an exclusive distributorship ("exclusive distributor") with no product/territory/time cap and no minimum performance targets, and further obligates SIERRA to cease sales to customers who violate ENVISION's exclusivity. This conflicts with the no-exclusivity position, whose preferred stance is a fully non-exclusive arrangement and whose fallback permits exclusivity only if limited to named products, named territory, max 12 months, and lapsing on failure to meet minimum performance targets. The clause states products, territory, and best-efforts requirements by cross-reference, but no term limit or minimum performance targets are present, and the agreement's stated effort standard (best efforts) does not supply the missing lapse trigger. Material exposure and a missing critical protection: no cap on exclusivity duration or performance-based lapse. A capped exclusivity may be negotiable if duration and minimum targets are added.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is non-exclusive. Each party remains free to provide to, procure from, or contract with any third party for services of the same or a similar kind, without restriction and without any obligation to the other party.

Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.
reviews.verification_reason: The assessment is supported by the clause and cited playbook. The clause does create an exclusive distributorship ('appoints ENVISION as its exclusive distributor,' limited to the Product in any blend with Krill Oil within the Territory), so the exclusivity claim is grounded. The policy positions are correctly contrasted: the preferred stance is fully non-exclusive, and the fallback permits exclusivity only if limited to named products, named territory, max 12 months, and lapsing on failure to meet minimum performance targets. The clause references products and territory and imposes 'best efforts' requirements by cross-reference to Sections 4, 5, and 9, but it contains no term/duration limit and no minimum performance targets or performance-based lapse trigger; that supports the rationale that the fallback conditions are not met. The rationale distinguishes contract text from policy requirements. Although 'best efforts' is not identical to 'minimum performance targets,' the rationale explicitly notes that best efforts does not supply the missing lapse trigger, which is a fair reading. The high risk level follows from conflict with a high-risk-if-absent no-exclusivity policy position. The suggested fallback matches the cited playbook fallback text verbatim.

clause.text: 3. Territory. The Territory shall be the entire world.
clause.heading: 3. Territory. The Territory shall be the entire world.

reviews.rationale: The clause merely sets the Territory as the entire world and contains no substantive obligation. The retrieved positions concern non-compete scope, licence duration, exclusivity, liquidated damages, and confidentiality survival — none of which are engaged by a bare territorial definition. The relevant questions (e.g., whether an unbounded territory makes any non-compete or exclusivity-related restriction in this Agreement impermissibly broad) turn on other clauses not provided. The non-compete-bounded position is framed as a non-compete obligation and does not itself restrict an unrelated territory definition; absent evidence of a non-compete or exclusivity obligation in this Agreement, applying its territory limitation would be manufacturing a risk. No supplied position supports a supported risk assessment on this standalone text.
reviews.verification_reason: assessment has no playbook citations supporting its risk and rationale

ENVISION shall not resell the Product alone. Terms of payment will be 1/3 upon placement of order and 2/3 balance net thirty (30) days or as mutually agreed upon in writing between the parties. Delivery will be F.O.B. ENVISION shall be responsible for all costs of shipping from SIERRA to ENVISION.

reviews.rationale: The clause sets the balance payment at net thirty (30) days, which matches the preferred net-30 timeline in the payment policy, and grants 90 days' advance notice of price changes. However, it permits SIERRA to raise prices to maximize profits and imposes a 1/3 upfront payment not addressed by the policy, and it omits any right to withhold disputed amounts in good faith. The deviation from the payment policy's dispute-withholding protection is a limited, negotiable exposure rather than a prohibition breach.

The medium risk level is consistent with the playbook's 'Risk if absent: medium'. The suggested fallback matches the cited fallback text verbatim.

clause.text:
5. Product Support. ENVISION will use its best efforts to market and sell the Finished Product throughout the Territory. The parties also agree that:

 o If SIERRA customers are interested in purchasing the Product in any blend with Krill Oil, SIERRA will refer them to ENVISION.

clause.heading: 5. Product Support. ENVISION will use its best efforts to market and sell the Finished Product throughout the Territory. The parties also agree that:

reviews.rationale: The clause imposes marketing efforts, a customer referral arrangement, and allocation of development/manufacturing costs. It creates no exclusivity: ENVISION must use best efforts to market and sell, but is not prohibited from dealing with third parties, so the no-exclusivity preferred position is met. No non-compete, employee non-solicit, IP ownership, joint-ownership, or renewal term is created by this clause, so those positions are not implicated. The clause does not address ownership of jointly developed intellectual property, but it also creates no joint development or joint ownership, so the absence of an IP ownership term here is a missing protection outside this clause's scope rather than a breach. Uncertainty: the clause is silent on whether referring SIERRA customers to ENVISION is reciprocal or requires any compensation; this is a commercial detail, not a policy deviation.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is non-exclusive. Each party remains free to provide to, procure from, or contract with any third party for services of the same or a similar kind, without restriction and without any obligation to the other party.

reviews.verification_reason: The assessment accurately reflects the clause text: Section 5 imposes marketing best efforts, a customer referral arrangement, and responsibility for development/manufacturing costs, and contains no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, IP ownership, joint-ownership, or renewal terms. These features support the claim that the no-exclusivity preferred position is met because the clause does not restrict either party from dealing with third parties. The rationale properly distinguishes what the clause states from what policy requests and does not assert unsupported contract or policy terms. No fallback is suggested, which is appropriate since the preferred position is met (and the cited fallback would not apply verbatim). The risk level of low follows from the comparison: the high-risk position is only triggered 'if absent,' and the clause effectively satisfies the preferred non-exclusive position rather than omitting it. The noted uncertainty about reciprocity or compensation is explicitly framed as a commercial detail, not a policy deviation, and is supported by the clause's silence.

clause.text: 6. Sales Disclosures. ENVISION will provide SIERRA with demand projections for the Product and SIERRA will produce enough Product to meet such demand projections. ENVISION will inform SIERRA of committed sales and SIERRA will increase or scale up its production of the Product accordingly. SIERRA will not unreasonably withhold the Product, but shall not be liable for unfulfilled or partially fulfilled orders given just cause for such action.
clause.heading: 6. Sales Disclosures. ENVISION will provide SIERRA with demand projections for the Product and SIERRA will produce enough Product to meet such demand projections. ENVISION will inform SIERRA of committed sales and SIERRA will increase or scale up its production of the Product accordingly. SIERRA will not unreasonably withhold the Product, but shall not be liable for unfulfilled or partially fulfilled orders given just cause for such action.

reviews.rationale: Clause 6 creates a forward-looking supply and demand-forecast obligation: ENVISION provides demand projections and SIERRA must scale production to meet them. This is an upside/downside volume commitment mechanism without the playbook's required protections — no minimum purchase or volume cap, no cap tied to a written commitment, and no limitation that liability for any shortfall is only the difference between committed and actual volume. The playbook position requires that any minimum purchase commitment be stated in an Order Form and that the customer's sole shortfall liability be the committed-versus-actual difference, with risk_if_absent rated high. Because the clause imposes production scale-up obligations tied to ENVISION's projections without those guardrails, it fails the relevant preferred position and exposes SIERRA to uncapped production/volume risk. The clause's liability carve-out ('shall not be liable for unfulfilled or partially fulfilled orders given just cause') is a narrow exception and does not cure the missing commitment limits. Note: the clause does not specify whether SIERRA is the supplier or customer in this arrangement, and the provided positions do not otherwise address demand-forecast or production-scale obligations, so the assessment is grounded only on the no-minimum-commitment position most relevant to the volume/payment obligations in this payment_terms clause.

citations.excerpt: Customer is under no obligation to purchase any minimum quantity, value or share of its requirements under this Agreement, and shall pay only for the Services it actually orders.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any minimum purchase commitment under this Agreement shall be stated in the applicable Order Form, shall not exceed the amount Customer committed to in writing, and Customer's sole liability for a shortfall shall be to pay the difference between the committed and the actual volume.
reviews.verification_reason: The clause text supports the reviewer's description: ENVISION provides demand projections, SIERRA must produce/scale up to meet them, and there is a narrow liability carve-out for just cause. The cited no-minimum-commitment position is accurately characterized (no minimum purchase, Order Form statement, committed-vs-actual shortfall liability, risk_if_absent high), and the fallback is quoted verbatim from the playbook. The high risk level follows from the gap between the clause's production/volume obligations and the playbook's required commitment limits and shortfall-liability cap. The rationale appropriately distinguishes clause language from policy requirements and acknowledges the limited scope/relevance of the cited position.

clause.text: 7. Term. The term of this Agreement shall be two (2) years from the Effective Date with automatic annual renewals thereafter provided either party does not provide sixty (60) days notice of termination prior to the renewal date or the Agreement is not otherwise terminated as set forth in Section 8.
clause.heading: 7. Term. The term of this Agreement shall be two (2) years from the Effective Date with automatic annual renewals thereafter provided either party does not provide sixty (60) days notice of termination prior to the renewal date or the Agreement is not otherwise terminated as set forth in Section 8.

reviews.rationale: The clause provides for automatic successive 12-month renewals with non-renewal notice of 60 days, which deviates from the renewal-opt-in preferred position (renewal only by mutual written agreement) but partially satisfies the fallback mechanism of successive 12-month terms with notice-based non-renewal. However, the 60-day notice exceeds the fallback's minimum 30-day requirement, a limited deviation that is negotiable. The clause contains no termination-for-convenience right; it only provides a non-renewal notice mechanism, which is distinct from a right to terminate mid-term, so the termination-for-convenience fallback's 60-day convenience notice cannot be conflated with this non-renewal window. The absence of any convenience-termination right leaves the parties locked in for the full two-year initial term absent Section 8 events, and the clause contains no cap or indexation on renewal fees, leaving pricing exposure unaddressed relative to the price-increase-capped position. Because the fallback renewal-opt-in terms are substantially met on term length and only the 60-day non-renewal notice deviates from the 30-day fallback minimum, and because the missing convenience termination is treated as a medium risk-if-absent under the playbook, the aggregate exposure remains medium rather than high, though the notice period and pricing gap should be negotiated.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement shall renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term, and the fees for any renewal term shall not increase by more than five percent (5%).

Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party, without penalty or further liability other than for amounts accrued prior to the effective date of termination.

Fees are fixed for the Initial Term. Supplier may increase fees for a renewal term by no more than the increase in the consumer price index over the preceding term, on at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice.

reviews.suggested_fallback: This Agreement shall renew for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the then-current term, and the fees for any renewal term shall not increase by more than five percent (5%).
reviews.verification_reason: The assessment is largely accurate on contract facts but contains a policy-comparison error and a mischaracterization. (1) The rationale says the clause 'partially satisfies the fallback mechanism' and that the 60-day notice 'exceeds the fallback's minimum 30-day requirement, a limited deviation that is negotiable.' This misapplies the fallback: a 60-day non-renewal notice is more favorable to the non-renewing party than the fallback's 30-day minimum, so it is not a risk deviation; it does not support a deviation rationale. (2) The rationale conflates the renewal-opt-in fallback with price terms, treating the 'no cap or indexation on renewal fees' as a separate gap, when the cited renewal-opt-in fallback itself contains the 5% fee-cap language; the price-increase-capped position is a distinct policy and should be assessed on its own. (3) The suggested fallback matches the renewal-opt-in fallback verbatim and is properly attributed. (4) The risk level of medium is defensible under the playbook (each position's risk-if-absent is medium), so the conclusion is not clearly contradicted, but the reasoning overstates a non-deviation and misattributes the fee-cap gap. Correction: omit the claim that the 60-day notice exceeds the fallback and is a deviation; instead note it is more protective than the fallback and thus acceptable. Assess the absent fee cap under [price-increase-capped] rather than folding it into [renewal-opt-in], and assess the absent convenience-termination right under [termination-for-convenience] as its own medium risk-if-absent gap.

clause.text:
8. Termination. (a) Upon the occurrence of a material breach or default as to any obligation, term or provision contained herein by either party and the failure of the breaching party to promptly pursue (within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice thereof from the non-breaching party) a reasonable remedy designed to cure (in the reasonable judgment of the non-breaching party) such material breach or default, this Agreement may be terminated by the non-breaching party by giving written notice of termination to the breaching party, such termination

 being immediately effective upon the giving of such notice of termination.

 (b) Upon the occurrence of bankruptcy of the other party, breach of confidentiality, government legislative interference, or force majeure extending beyond sixty (60) days, either party may immediately terminate the Agreement.
clause.heading: 8. Termination. (a) Upon the occurrence of a material breach or default as to any obligation, term or provision contained herein by either party and the failure of the breaching party to promptly pursue (within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice thereof from the non-breaching party) a reasonable remedy designed to cure (in the reasonable judgment of the non-breaching party) such material breach or default, this Agreement may be terminated by the non-breaching party by giving written notice of termination to the breaching party, such termination

reviews.rationale: Clause 8(a) anchors termination for cause to a cure period, but the 30-day window is conditioned on the breaching party 'promptly pursu[ing]' a 'reasonable remedy designed to cure' in the non-breaching party's reasonable judgment, rather than simply failing to actually cure within the period. This is a limited deviation from the preferred termination-for-cause-cure position, creating residual exposure to premature termination and a lower threshold than a completed cure. Clause 8(b) separately allows immediate termination for breaches or events (bankruptcy, confidentiality breach, legislative interference) and for force majeure beyond 60 days. The force majeure trigger is consistent with the fallback force-majeure-bounded position, which permits termination after 60 days. No termination-for-convenience right is provided, but that absence is not itself departures from the clause's stated for-cause scheme.

citations.excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.

Neither party is liable for a failure to perform caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, provided it notifies the other party promptly and resumes performance as soon as practicable. Force majeure does not excuse an obligation to pay amounts already due, and either party may terminate if the event continues for more than sixty (60) days.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause if the other party materially breaches it and fails to cure that breach within forty-five (45) days after receiving written notice describing the breach in reasonable detail.
reviews.verification_reason: The assessment is supported. The clause text confirms 8(a)'s cure period is conditioned on the breaching party promptly pursuing a reasonable remedy rather than completing an actual cure, and that judgment rests with the non-breaching party — a fair characterization of the clause. This is accurately compared to the preferred 30-day 'fails to cure' standard, justifying a medium-risk limited deviation. Clause 8(b)'s immediate termination triggers and the 60-day force majeure threshold are correctly quoted, and the 60-day figure matches the [force-majeure-bounded] fallback verbatim. The suggested fallback reproduces the [termination-for-cause-cure] fallback text exactly (45 days, same wording). The rationale distinguishes clause language from playbook positions and the risk level follows from the comparison.

clause.heading: 10. Intellectual Property. SIERRA is responsible for all Patent costs for the Product. SIERRA warrants it owns pending patents for the Product in the U.S. and internationally. SIERRA hereby grants ENVISION an exclusive, royalty-free sub-license of the Product's future patents, and patent applications to distribute, sell and market the Finished Product. SIERRA hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold ENVISION harmless from any claims that the Product infringes upon any other patent.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants ENVISION an exclusive, royalty-free sub-license of the Product's future patents and patent applications, creating an exclusive dealing commitment. The relevant playbook position requires non-exclusivity or, at most, narrowly limited exclusivity (named products/territory, max 12 months, performance-target lapse). This clause contains none of those limits, and it is stated as an indeterminate, royalty-free exclusive license. The clause also includes a one-sided IP infringement indemnity from SIERRA to ENVISION; the mutual-indemnity position expects each party to indemnify for its own breach/negligence (or at least gross negligence/willful misconduct), so the one-sided broad indemnity deviates from policy, though it is the exclusivity term that is the material exposure.

citations.excerpt: This Agreement is non-exclusive. Each party remains free to provide to, procure from, or contract with any third party for services of the same or a similar kind, without restriction and without any obligation to the other party.

Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.

Each party shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the other party against third-party claims to the extent arising from its own breach of this Agreement or its negligence, subject to the limitations of liability set out in this Agreement.

Supplier shall defend and indemnify Customer against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe that third party's intellectual property rights, and shall pay any damages finally awarded or agreed in settlement.

reviews.suggested_fallback: Any exclusivity granted under this Agreement is limited to the named products, the named territory and a period of no more than twelve (12) months, and lapses if the exclusive party fails to meet the minimum performance targets stated in the Order Form.

The one-sided SIERRA-to-ENVISION indemnity is accurately contrasted with the mutual-indemnity position. The suggested fallback matches the [no-exclusivity] fallback text verbatim. Risk level of high follows from the high-risk exclusivity gap.

Upon termination, ENVISION shall have eighteen (18) months to exhaust any inventories, packaging and advertising materials bearing the "SierraSil" trademark and SIERRA shall have first option to buy back any inventory at ENVISION's net purchase price.

reviews.rationale: The clause grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free trademark licence and reserves SIERRA's ownership, which is consistent with a limited-scope grant and with the principle that the licensor retains its own IP. However, it deviates from the cited [licence-scope-limited] position: the licence is not stated to be non-transferable or revocable, and there is no automatic termination on expiry or termination. Instead, ENVISION receives an 18-month post-termination sell-off period and SIERRA has a first option to buy back inventory. This is a limited, negotiable deviation rather than a critical failure: exclusivity, ownership and royalty treatment are acceptable, but the missing non-transferability/revocability and the sell-off instead of automatic termination create residual exposure. The cited [ip-each-party-keeps-its-own] position is only tangentially relevant because it addresses each party retaining its own background IP, not merely a licensor retaining its trademark; it does not independently support 'low' risk.
